decision: The script that changes a task's record also makes the paired backlog change, in the same process and before it reports success.
alternatives: A later agent turn moves the backlog item.
A printed reminder asks the agent to move the item.
tradeoff: Spawn and teardown refuse rather than report success when the backlog transition cannot land, so a backlog fault can stop a dispatch or a cleanup.
reversal_cost: High in effect: spawn, teardown and bootstrap all rely on the pairing (inferred from the cited header, not stated by the authors).

decision: Isolated work is dispatched at once with no concurrency cap; overlap is a risk signal, not a reason to wait.
alternatives: Wait for overlapping work to finish (the cited text rejects same-file editing alone as a reason to serialize).
tradeoff: More parallel work and more rebases or conflicts for the delivery path to reconcile; the cited text accepts this when each change can be validated alone.
reversal_cost: Low (inferred): the rule is prose, and a declared project capacity already caps it in code.

decision: A spawn that cannot take the shared project lock exits at once instead of waiting.
alternatives: Wait for the lock until it is free.
tradeoff: The caller sees an error and must try again, but a stuck holder cannot hang the spawn (inferred).
reversal_cost: Low (inferred): one acquire call and its error branch.
